problems.title: Dispensing liquids with a volumetric pipet
problems.problem:
Question 12 (Local Section Exam, multiple choice).

Which is the best way to dispense liquids using a volumetric pipet?
(A) The pipet is immersed in the liquid to be dispensed, then lifted with a gloved finger on the top and the liquid allowed to drain to the mark. The remaining contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container.
(B) The pipet is immersed in the liquid to be dispensed, then lifted with a gloved finger on the top and the liquid allowed to drain to the mark. The remaining contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container, with a pipet bulb used to gently blow out any residual droplets.
(C) The tip of the pipet is submerged below the surface of the liquid and suction is applied using a pipet bulb until the liquid rises above the level of the mark. A gloved finger is then applied to the top of the pipet and the liquid allowed to drain to the mark. The remaining contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container.
(D) The tip of the pipet is submerged below the surface of the liquid and suction is applied by mouth until the liquid rises to the level of the mark. The contents are then allowed to drain into the desired container.

problems.title: Mechanism consistent with a tert-butyl chloride rate law
problems.problem:
Question 30 (Local Section Exam, multiple choice).

$\textit{Tert}$-butyl alcohol reacts with aqueous hydrochloric acid to give $\textit{tert}$-butyl chloride.
$$\ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + H+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq) + H2O(l)}$$
For this reaction, $\text{Rate} = k[\ce{(CH3)3COH}][\ce{H+}]$. With which mechanism is this rate law consistent?
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|r|}\hline \text{(A)} & \ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + H+(aq) <=> (CH3)3C(OH2)+(aq)} & \textit{fast} \\  & \ce{(CH3)3C(OH2)+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq) + H2O(l)} & \textit{slow} \\ \hline \text{(B)} & \ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + H+(aq) <=> (CH3)3C(OH2)+(aq)} & \textit{fast} \\  & \ce{(CH3)3C(OH2)+(aq) -> (CH3)3C+(aq) + H2O(l)} & \textit{slow} \\  & \ce{(CH3)3C+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq)} & \textit{fast} \\ \hline \text{(C)} & \ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq) + OH-(aq)} & \textit{slow} \\  & \ce{OH-(aq) + H+(aq) -> H2O(l)} & \textit{fast} \\ \hline \text{(D)} & \ce{(CH3)3COH(aq) -> (CH3)3C+(aq) + OH-(aq)} & \textit{slow} \\  & \ce{(CH3)3C+(aq) + Cl-(aq) -> (CH3)3CCl(aq)} & \textit{fast} \\  & \ce{OH-(aq) + H+(aq) -> H2O(l)} & \textit{fast} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

problems.problem:
Problem 1 (National Exam Part II).

Studtite is a mineral that contains only hydrogen, oxygen, and a metal $\mathrm{M}$. Its empirical formula is $\mathrm{MO}_x(\mathrm{H_2O})_y$, where $x$ and $y$ are integers.

A $1.0000\,\mathrm{g}$ sample of studtite is heated at $520\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, which causes it to decompose to molecular oxygen, water vapor, and the solid metal trioxide $\ce{MO3}$. The gases from this reaction are collected in a rigid container with a volume of $1.000\,\mathrm{L}$. When this container is maintained at $200.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the pressure is $355.0\,\mathrm{mm\,Hg}$. When the container is cooled to $25.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, some of the water vapor condenses to the liquid, and the pressure in the container falls to $48.65\,\mathrm{mm\,Hg}$. The vapor pressure of water at $25.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $23.80\,\mathrm{mm\,Hg}$.

a. Calculate the number of moles of $\ce{O2}$ produced in this reaction.

b. Calculate the number of moles of $\ce{H2O}$ produced in this reaction.

c. Calculate the mass of solid $\ce{MO3}$ produced in this reaction.

d. What is the identity of the metal $\mathrm{M}$? Support your answer.

e. What is the oxidation state of the metal $\mathrm{M}$ in the mineral studtite? Explain your answer.

problems.title: Barium iodate Ksp and calcium iodate thermodynamics
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (National Exam Part II).

Group 2 iodates such as $\ce{Ca(IO3)2}$ and $\ce{Ba(IO3)2}$ are sparingly soluble compounds.

The $K_\mathrm{sp}$ of $\ce{Ba(IO3)2}$ is measured by the following experiment: An aqueous solution is saturated with $\ce{Ba(IO3)2}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ and a $10.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ aliquot of this solution (free of any solid) is added to a solution containing an excess of $\ce{KI}$ in $1\,\mathrm{M}$ aqueous $\ce{HCl}$, causing the solution to turn yellow. This yellow solution is then titrated with $0.0150\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{Na2S2O3}$ solution until the color disappears; $8.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the thiosulfate solution is required to reach this endpoint.

a. Write balanced net ionic equations for

i. the reaction of the saturated $\ce{Ba(IO3)2}$ solution with the acidified $\ce{KI}$ solution; and

ii. the reaction of the yellow solution with the sodium thiosulfate solution.

b. Calculate the $K_\mathrm{sp}$ of $\ce{Ba(IO3)2}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$.

The $K_\mathrm{sp}$ of $\ce{Ca(IO3)2}$ can be measured by similar experiments. Below is shown a plot of $\ln(K_\mathrm{sp})$ of $\ce{Ca(IO3)2}$ as a function of $1/T$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2019-3-2-fig1.png

c. Calculate $\Delta H^\circ$ and $\Delta S^\circ$ for the dissolution of $\ce{Ca(IO3)2}$ in the range of $T = 273$ to $317\,\mathrm{K}$.

d. The $\ln(K_\mathrm{sp})$ vs. $1/T$ plot has a break in the curve because the stable crystalline form of calcium iodate changes in the temperature range shown. At some temperatures, the stable form is anhydrous $\ce{Ca(IO3)2}$, while at other temperatures the hexahydrate $\ce{Ca(IO3)2.6H2O}$ is the stable form. Assign which form is stable at which temperatures, and justify your assignment.

problems.title: Electrochemical synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (National Exam Part II).

There is considerable interest in producing ammonia by electrolyzing nitrogen/water mixtures (in the presence of suitable catalysts) as shown below.

$$\ce{N2(g) + 3 H2O(l) -> 2 NH3(g) + 1.5 O2(g)}$$

a. Would ammonia be evolved at the cathode or the anode of this electrolytic cell?

b. Calculate the standard cell potential $E^\circ$ for this reaction at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ given the thermodynamic data shown.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Compound} & \ce{H2O(l)} & \ce{NH3(g)} \\
\hline
\Delta G^\circ_\mathrm{f},\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} & -237.1 & -16.4 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

c. Would $E^\circ$ for this reaction be larger or smaller in magnitude at higher temperatures? Justify your answer.

d. The standard reduction potential of $\ce{O2}$ \textit{in acidic solution} is $1.23\,\mathrm{V}$.

$$\ce{O2(g) + 4 H+(aq) + 4 e- -> 2 H2O} \qquad E^\circ = 1.23\,\mathrm{V}$$

Write the half-reaction corresponding to the reduction of $\ce{O2(g)}$ to water in \textit{basic solution} and calculate the standard reduction potential.

e. Write the half-reaction corresponding to the reduction of $\ce{N2(g)}$ to $\ce{NH3(g)}$ in basic solution and calculate the standard reduction potential.

f. A cell for forming $\ce{NH3}$ by electrolysis of nitrogen as described above runs for $3000\,\mathrm{s}$ with a current of $1.20\,\mathrm{A}$ and produces $1.05 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{NH3}$. What is the faradaic yield of ammonia (that is, the yield of ammonia as a percentage of the maximum amount that could be formed by passage of this amount of electricity)?

problems.title: Kinetics of ascorbic acid oxidation by ferricyanide
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (National Exam Part II).

Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C, abbreviated $\mathrm{HAsc}$) is a weak acid with $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 4.10$. It is readily oxidized to form dehydroascorbic acid. One reagent that can carry out this oxidation is the ferricyanide ion, $\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2019-3-4-fig1.png

a. Write a balanced net ionic equation for the reaction of $\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}$ with $\mathrm{HAsc}$ in acidic solution.

The rate of this reaction can be followed by measuring $[\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}]$ through its absorbance at $416\,\mathrm{nm}$, where bright yellow $\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}$ absorbs light strongly and all the other colorless components of the reaction do not. Two runs were conducted with $[\ce{H+}] = 0.06\,\mathrm{M}$ and an initial $[\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}] = 5.22 \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{M}$, but with different $\mathrm{HAsc}$ concentrations. Plots of $\ln([\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}])$ as a function of time for the two runs are shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2019-3-4-fig2.png

b. What is the rate law for this reaction at $[\ce{H+}] = 0.06\,\mathrm{M}$? Explain your reasoning.

c. What is the rate constant for this reaction at $[\ce{H+}] = 0.06\,\mathrm{M}$? Make sure to include units.

The behavior of the reaction varies with the acidity of the solution. Five runs were conducted at $[\mathrm{HAsc}] = 0.00507\,\mathrm{M}$ and an initial $[\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}] = 5.22 \times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{M}$, but at varying $[\ce{H+}]$. For each run, $\ln([\ce{Fe(CN)6^{3-}}])$ was plotted as a function of time and the slope of the plot was measured. The slope was multiplied by $-1$ and its variation as a function of $[\ce{H+}]$ is graphed below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2019-3-4-fig3.png

d. Propose a mechanistic explanation for the effect of $[\ce{H+}]$ on the reaction kinetics. Be sure to explain how your mechanistic explanation qualitatively predicts the appearance of the plot.

problems.title: Borazine and related boron-nitrogen compounds
problems.problem:
Problem 7 (National Exam Part II).

Borazine, $\ce{B3N3H6}$, has a structure consisting of a six-membered ring with alternating $\ce{BH}$ and $\ce{NH}$ groups.

a. Draw a Lewis structure for borazine, including nonzero formal charges if needed. Show all major resonance structures of borazine.

b. Two other compounds containing boron, nitrogen, and hydrogen are $\ce{BH3NH3}$ and $\ce{BH2NH2}$. Draw Lewis structures for these two compounds, again including any formal charges and major resonance structures.

c. The $\ce{B-N}$ distances in $\ce{B3N3H6}$, $\ce{BH3NH3}$, and $\ce{BH2NH2}$ are $139.1$, $142.9$, and $156.4\,\mathrm{pm}$ (not necessarily in that order). Assign each $\ce{B-N}$ distances to the proper compound and explain your reasoning.

d. Typically, when one replaces a hydrogen attached to $\ce{N}$ with a $\ce{CH3}$ group, the boiling point of the compound decreases. For example, piperazine has a normal boiling point of $146\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ while $N$-methylpiperazine has a normal boiling point of $138\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Explain this observation.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2019-3-7-fig1.png

e. problems.title: Mond process for nickel tetracarbonyl
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (National Exam Part II).

The Mond process was used in the late 19th and early 20th centuries to purify nickel metal away from impurities such as iron and cobalt. The process relies on the facile reaction of nickel with carbon monoxide to form volatile nickel tetracarbonyl, which can be separated from the solid impurities:

$$\ce{Ni(s) + 4 CO(g) -> Ni(CO)4(g)}$$

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
 & \ce{Ni(s)} & \ce{Ni(g)} & \ce{CO(g)} & \ce{Ni(CO)4(g)} \\
\hline
\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{f}\ (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) & 0 & 430.1 & -110.5 & -607 \\
\hline
S^\circ\ (\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}) & 30 & 182.2 & 198 & 417 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. Draw or clearly describe the three-dimensional arrangement of the atoms in $\ce{Ni(CO)4}$.

b. Calculate the average bond dissociation enthalpy for the nickel-carbon bonds in $\ce{Ni(CO)4(g)}$.

c. Calculate $\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{rxn}$ and $\Delta S^\circ_\mathrm{rxn}$ for the production of $\ce{Ni(CO)4(g)}$ by the Mond process.

d. The boiling point of $\ce{Ni(CO)4}$ at $1\,\mathrm{bar}$ pressure is $42\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and its heat of vaporization is $29.0\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. Calculate $\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{f}$ and $S^\circ$ for $\ce{Ni(CO)4(l)}$.

e. After the $\ce{Ni(CO)4}$ vapor has been separated from the solid impurities, $\ce{Ni}$ metal is recovered by heating the $\ce{Ni(CO)4}$ to high temperature, causing it to re-form nickel metal and carbon monoxide. At $230\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, what is the equilibrium pressure of $\ce{Ni(CO)4(g)}$ in the presence of nickel metal, assuming that the carbon monoxide pressure is maintained at $0.10\,\mathrm{bar}$?

problems.title: Kinetics of bromine monoxide decomposition
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (National Exam Part II).

Gas-phase bromine monoxide, $\ce{BrO}$, decomposes according to two possible pathways:

$$\ce{2 BrO(g) -> O2(g) + 2 Br(g)} \qquad (4a)$$

$$\ce{2 BrO(g) -> O2(g) + Br2(g)} \qquad (4b)$$

The reaction can be studied by generating $\ce{BrO(g)}$ by using a laser. If this is carried out in the presence of excess ozone, then any $\ce{Br(g)}$ that is present reacts with ozone to produce bromine monoxide much more rapidly than either reaction 4a or 4b.

$$\ce{Br(g) + O3(g) -> BrO(g) + O2(g)} \qquad \textit{fast}$$

The disappearance of $\ce{BrO(g)}$ was studied spectrophotometrically at both $267\,\mathrm{K}$ and $298\,\mathrm{K}$, either in the absence of excess ozone (open squares) or in the presence of excess ozone (open circles). The reciprocal of the concentration of $\ce{BrO}$ as a function of time is graphed below for the four experiments.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2020-3-4-fig1.png

a. What is the reaction order in $\ce{BrO}$ for its decomposition in the absence of $\ce{O3}$? Justify your answer based on the experimental data.

b. A sample of $\ce{BrO}$ in $\ce{N2}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ with an initial concentration of $4.0 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{molecules\,cm^{-3}}$ is prepared. How much time will it take for the $\ce{BrO}$ concentration to decay to half its original value?

c. Is the observed decomposition of $\ce{BrO}$ faster or slower in the presence of ozone? Justify your answer based on the experimental data and provide a chemical explanation for the observed difference.

d. Calculate the values of $k_\mathrm{4a}$ and $k_\mathrm{4b}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$.

e. Calculate the activation energy for the decomposition of $\ce{BrO}$ in the presence of ozone.

Problem 6 (National Exam Part II).

A solution is made by adding some $\ce{CuSO4.5H2O}$ to water, followed by enough sulfuric acid to make the $\mathrm{pH} = 1.00$. Two platinum electrodes are then placed in the solution (which has a total volume of $0.500\,\mathrm{L}$) and the solution is electrolyzed at a constant current of $0.120\,\mathrm{A}$, separately capturing any gases that are evolved at the two electrodes.

Initially, gas is evolved at the anode, but no gas is evolved at the cathode. However, after $10.0\,\mathrm{min}$ of electrolysis, gas evolution begins at the cathode as well, and eventually the total volume of gas evolved at the cathode is equal to the total volume of gas evolved at the anode.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c||c|c|}
\hline
\text{Half-Reaction} & E^\circ,\ \mathrm{V} & \text{Half-Reaction} & E^\circ,\ \mathrm{V} \\
\hline
\ce{Cu+(aq) + e- -> Cu(s)} & 0.518 & \ce{Cu^{2+}(aq) + 2 e- -> Cu(s)} & 0.337 \\
\hline
\ce{O2(g) + 2 H+(aq) + 2 e- -> H2O2(aq)} & 1.780 & \ce{O2(g) + 4 H+(aq) + 4 e- -> 2 H2O(l)} & 1.229 \\
\hline
\ce{2 H+(aq) + e- -> H2(g)} & 0.000 & & \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. Write the balanced reaction that takes place initially in this electrolytic cell.

b. How many moles of copper(II) sulfate pentahydrate were initially added to the solution?

c. What is the initial cell potential for this reaction at $298\,\mathrm{K}$? (In air, the partial pressure of $\ce{O2(g)}$ is $0.20\,\mathrm{bar}$ and the partial pressure of $\ce{H2(g)}$ may be taken to be $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{bar}$.)

d. As the electrolysis proceeds (before $t = 10.0\,\mathrm{min}$), will this cell potential become more positive, more negative, or remain unchanged? Explain your answer.

e. What gas is evolved at the anode? What gas is evolved at the cathode (after $t = 10.0\,\mathrm{min}$)?

f. At what time will the total volumes of evolved gases at the two electrodes be equal?

problems.title: NO2Cl and NO equilibrium thermodynamics
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (National Exam Part II).

The gas-phase equilibrium between nitryl chloride ($\ce{NO2Cl}$) and nitrosyl chloride ($\ce{NOCl}$) was studied:

$$\ce{NO2Cl(g) + NO(g) <=> NOCl(g) + NO2(g)} \qquad (4a)$$

The equilibrium constant for reaction 4a was measured as $K_\mathrm{4a} = 1.12 \times 10^{4}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ and $K_\mathrm{4a} = 4.68 \times 10^{3}$ at $340\,\mathrm{K}$.

a. Calculate $\Delta G^\circ_\mathrm{4a}$ at both $298\,\mathrm{K}$ and $340\,\mathrm{K}$.

b. Calculate $\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{4a}$ and $\Delta S^\circ_\mathrm{4a}$ (assuming that they are essentially independent of temperature).

c. Which of the four gaseous compounds involved in this equilibrium has the lowest standard molar entropy $S^\circ$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$? Justify your choice.

d. The normal boiling point of $\ce{NOCl}$ is $-6\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Consider reaction 4b that produces liquid $\ce{NOCl}$ rather than gaseous $\ce{NOCl}$:

$$\ce{NO2Cl(g) + NO(g) <=> NOCl(l) + NO2(g)} \qquad (4b)$$

At $298\,\mathrm{K}$, how will each of the thermodynamic quantities $\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{4b}$, $\Delta S^\circ_\mathrm{4b}$, and $\Delta G^\circ_\mathrm{4b}$ compare to the corresponding thermodynamic quantity for reaction 4a (i.e., will the quantity for 4b be greater than, less than, or equal to the quantity for 4a)? Justify your answers.

e. In experimental practice, the study of equilibrium 4a is complicated by the fact that $\ce{NO2(g)}$ is also in equilibrium with $\ce{N2O4(g)}$ according to reaction 4c under conditions where reaction 4a attains equilibrium.

$$\ce{2 NO2(g) <=> N2O4(g)} \qquad (4c)$$

Suppose that samples of $\ce{NO2Cl}$ and $\ce{NO}$ are introduced into a reaction vessel and the mixture is allowed to attain equilibrium according to reactions 4a and 4c at $320\,\mathrm{K}$. If the volume of the reaction vessel is doubled, will the number of moles of $\ce{NOCl(g)}$ increase, decrease, or stay the same after the system reattains equilibrium? Justify your answer.

problems.title: Chlorofluorocarbon of unknown formula
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (National Exam Part II).

Compound $\mathbf{A}$ contains only carbon, fluorine, and chlorine.

a. The vapor density of $\mathbf{A}$ at $1.00\,\mathrm{bar}$ and $25.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is $6.895\,\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$. What is the molar mass of $\mathbf{A}$?

b. Chlorofluorocarbons such as $\mathbf{A}$ react with sodium metal to convert all the chlorine present into sodium chloride. The products from the reaction of sodium with $100.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of gaseous $\mathbf{A}$ (at $1.00\,\mathrm{bar}$ and $25.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$) are dissolved in water and a few drops of sodium chromate solution are added. This solution is then titrated with $0.3540\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{AgNO3}$ solution until a bright red precipitate appears, which requires $22.79\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the titrant. How many chlorine atoms are there in a molecule of $\mathbf{A}$?

c. What is the molecular formula of $\mathbf{A}$? Justify your answer.

d. There is only one known isomer of $\mathbf{A}$, compound $\mathbf{B}$. The two compounds have nearly identical boiling points, but can be distinguished by $^{19}\mathrm{F}$ NMR spectroscopy, a technique that is sensitive to small differences in the chemical environments of fluorine atoms in compounds. When analyzed by this method, compound $\mathbf{A}$ exhibits only a single type of chemical environment for fluorine, while compound $\mathbf{B}$ shows two distinct environments for its fluorine atoms. Draw structural formulas for compounds $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ that are consistent with these observations.

problems.title: Ammonia/ammonium chloride buffer and silver chloride

b. What mole ratio of ammonia to ammonium chloride is required for the buffer to have $\mathrm{pH} = 9.20$?

c. Calculate the volume of ammonia solution and mass of ammonium chloride needed to make up $500\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the $\mathrm{pH} = 9.20$ buffer with a total concentration of nitrogen-containing species ($\ce{NH3}$ or $\ce{NH4+}$) of $0.50\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$.

d. To the solution described in (c) is added $10.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.10\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{AgNO3}$.

i. Some $\ce{AgCl}$ precipitates from this mixture. Justify that this is the case. The $K_\mathrm{sp}$ of $\ce{AgCl}$ is $1.8 \times 10^{-10}$ and the $K_\mathrm{f}$ of $\ce{Ag(NH3)2+}$ is $1.6 \times 10^{7}$.

ii. What is the final concentration of free $\ce{Ag+}$ in solution after this mixture achieves equilibrium?

iii. What is the mass of $\ce{AgCl}$ that precipitates from solution?

problems.title: Thermodynamics of molecular and atomic bromine
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (National Exam Part II).

Gaseous molecular and atomic bromine have the following thermodynamic properties:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Species} & \boldsymbol{\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{f}}\ \textbf{(kJ mol}^{-1}\textbf{)} & \boldsymbol{S^\circ}\ \textbf{(J mol}^{-1}\ \textbf{K}^{-1}\textbf{)} \\
\hline
\ce{Br2}(g) & 30.9 & 245.4 \\
\hline
\ce{Br}(g) & 111.9 & 175.0 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. What is the bond dissociation enthalpy (BDE) of the bromine-bromine bond in $\ce{Br2}(g)$?

b. How many atoms of $\ce{Br}(g)$ will be present at equilibrium in a $1.00\text{-L}$ container with $0.100\,\mathrm{bar}$ of $\ce{Br2}(g)$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$?

c. The ionization energy of $\ce{Br}(g)$ is $1145.9\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$, while the ionization energy of $\ce{Br2}(g)$ is $1025.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. What is the bond dissociation enthalpy of $\ce{Br2+}(g)$ (defined as the enthalpy of reaction of $\ce{Br2+}(g)$ to form $\ce{Br+}(g)$ and $\ce{Br}(g)$)?

d. Propose an explanation for the difference in BDE between $\ce{Br2}(g)$ and $\ce{Br2+}(g)$ in terms of the bonding in these two species.

e. The vapor pressure of liquid bromine at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ is $0.283\,\mathrm{bar}$. What is the absolute entropy $S^\circ$ of $\ce{Br2}(l)$?

f. The absolute entropies of the gas-phase atoms of the fourth period given in the table exhibit a non-monotonic pattern. Explain why the absolute entropies of $\ce{Se}(g)$ and $\ce{Br}(g)$ are larger than the absolute entropies of either $\ce{As}(g)$ or $\ce{Kr}(g)$.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
 & \ce{As}(g) & \ce{Se}(g) & \ce{Br}(g) & \ce{Kr}(g) \\
\hline
S^\circ,\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} & 163.2 & 176.7 & 175.0 & 164.1 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

problems.title: Iodide and hydrogen peroxide clock reaction
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (National Exam Part II).

Iodide ion reacts with hydrogen peroxide in acidic solution according to the following equation:

$$\ce{2 I-(aq) + H2O2(aq) + 2 H+(aq) -> I2(aq) + 2 H2O(l)} \qquad (4)$$

The reaction is carried out at $18.8\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in the presence of a mixture of $\ce{CH3COOH}$ and $\ce{NaOH}$ to regulate the pH, sodium thiosulfate (which reacts very rapidly with $\ce{I2}$ to form tetrathionate ions), and starch. All the components except the hydrogen peroxide are premixed, and then the hydrogen peroxide solution is added and a stopwatch is started. The solution remains colorless until it suddenly turns blue, at which point the time $t$ is recorded. The following data are obtained:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Run} & \begin{array}{c}1.0\,\mathrm{M}\\ \ce{CH3COOH},\\ \mathrm{mL}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}1.0\,\mathrm{M}\ \ce{NaOH},\\ \mathrm{mL}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}0.20\,\mathrm{M}\\ \ce{KI},\ \mathrm{mL}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}0.20\,\mathrm{M}\\ \ce{H2O2},\ \mathrm{mL}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}0.020\,\mathrm{M}\\ \ce{Na2S2O3},\\ \mathrm{mL}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}\text{Distilled}\\ \ce{H2O},\ \mathrm{mL}\end{array} & t,\ \mathrm{s} \\
\hline
\text{A} & 2.0 & 1.0 & 2.0 & 2.0 & 1.0 & 2.0 & 68.2 \\
\hline
\text{B} & 4.0 & 1.0 & 2.0 & 2.0 & 1.0 & 0.0 & 68.9 \\
\hline
\text{C} & 2.0 & 1.0 & 4.0 & 2.0 & 1.0 & 0.0 & 33.2 \\
\hline
\text{D} & 2.0 & 1.0 & 2.0 & 4.0 & 1.0 & 0.0 & 32.9 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. Give a qualitative explanation for why the solution suddenly turns blue after a certain amount of time has elapsed.

b. Calculate the initial $[\ce{H+}]$ in runs A and B and explain why $[\ce{H+}]$ will not change significantly over the course of the respective reactions. (The $K_\mathrm{a}$ of $\ce{CH3COOH}$ is $1.8 \times 10^{-5}$.)

c. The rate law for reaction (4) has the form $\mathrm{Rate} = k_4[\ce{I-}]^m[\ce{H2O2}]^n[\ce{H+}]^p$, where $m$, $n$, and $p$ are integers. What are the values of $m$, $n$, and $p$ under these experimental conditions? Briefly explain your reasoning.

d. What is the value of the rate constant $k_4$ for this reaction?

e. The following mechanism for reaction (4) has been proposed:

$$\begin{array}{lr}
\ce{H2O2(aq) + H+(aq) <=> H3O2+(aq)} & (\textit{fast, unfavorable}) \\
\ce{H3O2+(aq) + I-(aq) -> HOI(aq) + H2O(l)} & (\textit{slow}) \\
\ce{HOI(aq) + H+(aq) <=> H2OI+(aq)} & (\textit{fast, unfavorable}) \\
\ce{H2OI+(aq) + I-(aq) -> I2(aq) + H2O(l)} & (\textit{fast})
\end{array}$$

Is this mechanism consistent with the given data? Justify your answer.

f. The experiments are repeated under the same conditions as Runs A and B above, except that phosphoric acid ($\ce{H3PO4}$, $K_\mathrm{a} = 7.6 \times 10^{-3}$) is substituted for acetic acid. The observed times for the solutions to turn blue with this substitution are $46.7\,\mathrm{s}$ and $31.5\,\mathrm{s}$, respectively. Propose an interpretation for these observations.

A galvanic cell is constructed at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ with one half-cell consisting of a $10.00\,\mathrm{g}$ silver wire immersed in $1.00\,\mathrm{L}$ of a $0.100\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of silver nitrate and the second half-cell consisting of a $20.00\,\mathrm{g}$ copper plate immersed in $1.00\,\mathrm{L}$ of a $0.200\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of copper(II) sulfate.

problems.title: Ionic compound of hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (National Exam Part II).

$\mathbf{A}$ is an ionic compound that contains only the elements hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen.

a. A $1.000\text{-g}$ sample of $\mathbf{A}$ is dissolved in $20\,\mathrm{mL}$ water and titrated with $0.5000\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{NaOH}$ solution, giving the data shown below. What is the molar mass of $\mathbf{A}$?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2023-3-1-fig1.png

b. When a $1.000\text{-g}$ sample of $\mathbf{A}$ is heated at $230\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ in an evacuated $1.50\,\mathrm{L}$ vessel, it decomposes into gaseous products, giving a final pressure of $784\,\mathrm{mm\,Hg}$. How many moles of gas are formed in this reaction?

c. If the gases produced from the decomposition of $1.000\,\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathbf{A}$ are instead first passed through a column packed with magnesium perchlorate (which strongly absorbs water vapor) and then collected at $25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and a pressure of $755\,\mathrm{mm\,Hg}$, the total volume of gas is $308\,\mathrm{mL}$. How many moles of gas are collected in this experiment?

d. What is the formula of $\mathbf{A}$? Explain your reasoning.

e. Write Lewis structures for the cation and the anion present in $\mathbf{A}$ and for the product(s) of its decomposition at $230\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Your Lewis structures should include all bonds, lone pairs, and nonzero formal charges. You should show all significant resonance structures for each species.

problems.title: Acidity of aqua zinc ions and zinc hydroxide solubility
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (National Exam Part II).

When water is bound to a metal ion, its acidity increases. For example, the $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ of $\ce{Zn^{2+}}(aq)$ is $8.96$.

a. Calculate the pH of a $0.010\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of zinc nitrate, $\ce{Zn(NO3)2}$.

b. Calculate the pH of a $0.010\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of zinc acetate, $\ce{Zn(CH3COO)2}$. The $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}$ of $\ce{CH3COOH}$ is $4.75$.

c. Zinc hydroxide is sparingly soluble, with $K_\mathrm{sp} = 4.5 \times 10^{-17}$. Calculate the pH of a solution of water saturated with solid $\ce{Zn(OH)2}$.

d. Under what circumstances, if any, will a solution of zinc acetate spontaneously form a precipitate of $\ce{Zn(OH)2}$? If precipitation is possible, specify the circumstances under which it is spontaneous. If it is not possible, justify why not.

e. Zinc also forms a complex ion, $\ce{Zn(OH)4^{2-}}$, with $K_\mathrm{f} = 5.0 \times 10^{14}$. Calculate the solubility of $\ce{Zn(OH)2}$ in a solution with $\mathrm{pH} = 12.00$.

problems.title: Thermochemistry of hydrogen combustion
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (National Exam Part II).

Hydrogen gas reacts with oxygen gas to give water vapor with $\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{rxn} = -241.8\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\Delta S^\circ_\mathrm{rxn} = -44.5\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

$$\ce{H2}(g) + 0.5\,\ce{O2}(g) \rightarrow \ce{H2O}(g)$$

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Species} & S^\circ,\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} & C_\mathrm{p},\ \mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,K^{-1}} \\
\hline
\ce{H2O}(g) & ??? & 4.18 \\
\hline
\ce{H2}(g) & 130.7 & 14.4 \\
\hline
\ce{O2}(g) & 205.2 & 0.92 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. Calculate $S^\circ$ of $\ce{H2O}(g)$.

b. The bond dissociation enthalpy (BDE) of an average $\ce{O-H}$ bond in water is $463\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and the BDE of the $\ce{H-H}$ bond in $\ce{H2}$ is $436\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$. What is the BDE of the $\ce{O=O}$ bond in $\ce{O2}$?

c. $0.100\,\mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{H2}(g)$ and $0.100\,\mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{O2}(g)$, both initially at $100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, react completely in a sealed vessel that is maintained at $1\,\mathrm{bar}$ pressure. The vessel is machined as part of a $1.00\text{-kg}$ block of aluminum ($C_\mathrm{p} = 0.89\,\mathrm{J\,g^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$), which efficiently absorbs the heat generated in the reaction but which is well insulated from its surroundings. What is the final temperature of the aluminum block and the contents of the reaction vessel? Assume that $C_\mathrm{p}$ and $\Delta H^\circ_\mathrm{rxn}$ are independent of temperature.

d. Humid air at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ has an overall pressure of $1.0\,\mathrm{bar}$ and is $20.\,\mathrm{vol\%}$ $\ce{O2}$ and $3.1\,\mathrm{vol\%}$ $\ce{H2O}$. What is the minimum volume percentage of $\ce{H2}(g)$ in humid air necessary for its combustion to be spontaneous?

e. The lower flammability limit (LFL) of a substance is its minimum volumetric concentration needed to propagate a flame under a given set of conditions. The LFL of hydrogen gas in humid air is approximately $4\%$. Account for the difference between your answer in part d and the experimental value for the LFL.

problems.title: Vapor pressure and freezing of aqueous magnesium chloride
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (National Exam Part II).

The vapor pressure of pure water at its melting point, $0.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, is $611\,\mathrm{Pa}$ ($6.11 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{bar}$).

a. $0.880\,\mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{MgCl2}$ is added to $1.00\,\mathrm{kg}$ liquid water at $0.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Calculate the vapor pressure of this solution.

b. The enthalpy of sublimation of ice is $51.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ at $0.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and the enthalpy of vaporization of liquid water is $45.1\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ at $0.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Assuming these enthalpies are independent of temperature, calculate the temperature at which pure ice has the same vapor pressure as the magnesium chloride solution at $0.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ calculated in part a.

c. At the freezing point temperature of the aqueous magnesium chloride solution, the vapor pressure of the solution is equal to the vapor pressure of pure ice. Explain why this statement is true.

d. Using the principle enunciated in part c, calculate the freezing point temperature of the solution of $0.880\,\mathrm{mol}$ $\ce{MgCl2}$ dissolved in $1.00\,\mathrm{kg}$ water.

e. The temperature calculated in part d is the temperature of the system when the first solid appears at equilibrium as the system is cooled. As more solid is formed, do you expect the temperature to increase, decrease, or remain constant? Briefly justify your choice.

Write structural formulas for all organic substances, and clearly show stereochemistry where relevant. You need not balance the equations or show the phase of the species.

b. Aluminum foil is added to concentrated aqueous potassium hydroxide solution.

c. Metallic sodium is added to liquid ammonia in the presence of a trace amount of iron(III) nitrate.

e. Sodium tert-butoxide is added to 3-bromo-3-ethylpentane in $N,N$-dimethylformamide (DMF) solution.

problems.title: Platinum chloro complexes and an electrolytic cell
problems.problem:

The standard reduction potentials of some compounds of platinum and silver at $298\,\mathrm{K}$ are given below.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Half-reaction} & E^\circ,\ \mathrm{V} \\
\hline
\ce{Pt^{2+}}(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow \ce{Pt}(s) & +1.188 \\
\hline
\ce{PtCl4^{2-}}(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow \ce{Pt}(s) + 4\,\ce{Cl^-}(aq) & +0.758 \\
\hline
\ce{PtCl6^{2-}}(aq) + 2e^- \rightarrow \ce{PtCl4^{2-}}(aq) + 2\,\ce{Cl^-}(aq) & +0.726 \\
\hline
\ce{Ag^+}(aq) + e^- \rightarrow \ce{Ag}(s) & +0.799 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. What is $K_\mathrm{f}$ for the $\ce{PtCl4^{2-}}$ ion?

b. What is $E^\circ$ for the reduction of hexachloroplatinate(IV) to give platinum metal?

$$\ce{PtCl6^{2-}}(aq) + 4e^- \rightarrow \ce{Pt}(s) + 6\,\ce{Cl^-}(aq)$$

An electrolytic cell is set up as shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2023-3-6-fig1.png

c. What is the minimum potential that would need to be applied in order to cause the platinum electrode to dissolve to form $\ce{PtCl4^{2-}}(aq)$ and the $\ce{Ag^+}(aq)$ to deposit on the $\ce{Ag}$ electrode?

problems.title: Boiling points and bond lengths of fluorides and methyl compounds
problems.problem:
Problem 7 (National Exam Part II).

Fluorine atoms and methyl groups each form one bond, so there are often analogous compounds with the formulas $\ce{AF}_n$ and $\ce{A(CH3)}_n$. In the graphs below, the normal boiling points and the $\ce{A-X}$ bond distances of a series of $\ce{AX}_n$ molecules are compared ($\ce{A}$ = $2p$ element; $\ce{X}$ = $\ce{F}$ or $\ce{CH3}$).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2023-3-7-fig1.png

a. Draw or clearly describe the shapes of the molecules $\ce{BF3}$ and $\ce{NF3}$.

b. In all cases, the normal boiling points of the $\ce{AF}_n$ molecules are lower than those of the $\ce{A(CH3)}_n$ molecules. Explain this observation.

c. Not counting the boron compounds, the trend in boiling points is that they decrease as the central atom $\ce{A}$ moves to the right in the periodic table. Explain this trend.

d. Explain why $\ce{BF3}$ has a higher boiling point than $\ce{CF4}$, while $\ce{B(CH3)3}$ has a lower boiling point than $\ce{C(CH3)4}$.

e. Explain why the $\ce{A-C}$ bond distances decrease as $\ce{A}$ moves to the right in the periodic table.

f. Explain why the $\ce{A-F}$ bond distances increase as $\ce{A}$ moves to the right in the periodic table.

Problem 6 (National Exam Part II).

Consider the properties of the group 1 elements, whose valence shell electron configuration is $ns^1$, in the table below.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Element } M & n & \begin{array}{c}\text{First ionization}\\ \text{energy, kJ mol}^{-1}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}\text{Energy required to excite the valence}\\ \text{electron to the } (n+1)s \text{ orbital, kJ mol}^{-1}\end{array} & \begin{array}{c}\text{Molar density of}\\ \text{solid } M\text{Cl, mol cm}^{-3}\end{array} \\
\hline
\text{H} & 1 & 1312 & 984 & 0.0403 \\
\hline
\text{Li} & 2 & 520 & 325 & 0.0507 \\
\hline
\text{Na} & 3 & 496 & 308 & 0.0371 \\
\hline
\text{K} & 4 & 420 & 252 & 0.0266 \\
\hline
\text{Rb} & 5 & 403 & 241 & 0.0232 \\
\hline
\text{Cs} & 6 & 376 & 222 & 0.0237 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. Rationalize the observed trend in first ionization energies with increasing $n$.

b. Suppose a hydrogen atom were excited to its $2s^1$ state. If that excited state atom were to transfer its electron to $\ce{Cs+}$ to form a ground-state Cs atom, how much energy would that reaction absorb or release?

c. All but one of the atoms listed in the table have an excited state that is significantly lower in energy than the $(n+1)s^1$ state described in the table. Explain this observation, noting which atom is the exception and why.

d. All but one of the atoms listed in the table have an excited state that is modestly higher in energy ($38 - 55\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$) than the $(n+1)s^1$ state described in the table. Explain this observation, noting which atom is the exception and why.

e. The compounds $M\ce{Cl}(s)$ show a smooth decrease in their molar densities, except that $\ce{HCl}(s)$ is less dense than expected from the trend and $\ce{CsCl}(s)$ is more dense than expected. Explain this periodic trend, and give reasons for the two exceptions to the trend.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}
\hline
\textbf{Bond} & \textbf{BDE}\ (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) \\
\hline
\ce{C#C} & 839 \\
\hline
\ce{C-H} & 412 \\
\hline
\ce{O=O} & 498 \\
\hline
\ce{C=O} & 741 \\
\hline
\ce{O-H} & 463 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

$$\ce{C2H2(g) + 2.5 O2(g) -> 2 CO2(g) + H2O(g)} \qquad \Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{expt}} = -1256\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$$

(B) The tabulated $\ce{O=O}$ BDE does not account for the unusual weakness of the bond in dioxygen due to its paramagnetism.
(C) The tabulated $\ce{C=O}$ BDE does not account for the stabilization due to electronic delocalization in carbon dioxide.

problems.title: Combustion analysis and phase behaviour of an unknown compound
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (National Exam Part II).

An unknown compound $\mathbf{X}$ contains only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

a. When burned, $1.00\,\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathbf{X}$ produces $2.00\,\mathrm{g}$ of carbon dioxide and $0.818\,\mathrm{g}$ of water. What is the empirical formula of $\mathbf{X}$?

b. A $1.68\,\mathrm{g}$ sample of $\mathbf{X}$ is introduced into a $2.00\,\mathrm{L}$ evacuated flask. The flask is slowly heated until the liquid evaporates completely, which occurs at $62.3\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. At this temperature, the pressure in the flask is $200.0\,\mathrm{mmHg}$. What is the molar mass of $\mathbf{X}$, and what is its molecular formula?

c. The melting point of $\mathbf{X}$ is $11.8\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and its normal boiling point is $101.1\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Calculate the standard enthalpy and entropy of vaporization of $\mathbf{X}$.

d. What types of intermolecular forces are likely present in liquid $\mathbf{X}$? Justify your answer.

e. The unit cell of crystalline $\mathbf{X}$ at its melting point has a volume of $241.5\,\mathrm{\AA^3}$ and the density of the solid is $1.211\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$. How many molecules of $\mathbf{X}$ are present in the unit cell?

f. The density of liquid $\mathbf{X}$ at its melting point is $1.034\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$. Will the melting point increase, decrease, or stay the same as the pressure is increased?

c. To $1.00\,\mathrm{L}$ of a $0.01\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of $\ce{Ni(NO3)2}$ is slowly added ammonia. Initially, a green precipitate of $\ce{Ni(OH)2}$ ($K_{\mathrm{sp}} = 2.0 \times 10^{-15}$) is formed. What is the pH of the solution at the point where the precipitate just begins to form?

d. By the time $0.600\,\mathrm{mol}$ of $\ce{NH3}$ have been added to the solution in c., the solution has become homogeneous and violet in color. Calculate the concentration of $\ce{Ni^{2+}(aq)}$ in this solution.

e. Nickel sulfide is quite insoluble ($K_{\mathrm{sp}} = 4.0 \times 10^{-20}$). $0.010\,\mathrm{mol}$ of $\ce{NiS}$ is suspended in $1.00\,\mathrm{L}$ of a solution buffered at $\mathrm{pH} = 10.00$. Ammonia is then bubbled through this solution until the nickel sulfide just dissolves. Show that no solid $\ce{Ni(OH)2}$ will be present at this point. For $\ce{H2S}$, $\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a1}} = 7.05$ and $\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a2}} = 19.0$.

• a $\beta$ phase $\beta\text{-}\ce{LaNi5H}_{6.39}\ce{(s)}$ observed at higher $\ce{H2}$ pressure, characterized by metal-hydrogen bonding

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Species} & \Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{f}},\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} & S^\circ,\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} & \text{Species} & \Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{f}},\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}} & S^\circ,\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}} \\
\hline
\ce{H2(g)} & 0 & 130.7 & \ce{LaNi5(s)} & -162 & 217 \\
\ce{Ni(s)} & 0 & 29.9 & \alpha\text{-}\ce{LaNi5H}_{x}\ce{(s)} & -186 & 223 \\
\ce{La(s)} & 0 & 56.9 & \beta\text{-}\ce{LaNi5H}_{6.39}\ce{(s)} & ? & ? \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

a. Calculate $\Delta G^\circ_{\mathrm{f}}$ of $\ce{LaNi5(s)}$ at $298\,\mathrm{K}$.

$\ce{LaNi5(s)}$ is placed in vacuum chambers, one at $30.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and one at $50.0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. Pure $\ce{H2(g)}$ is added to each chamber, and the weight-percent hydrogenation of $\ce{LaNi5(s)}$ is recorded as a function of pressure.

problems.title: Hydrolysis of iodomethane: rate constants and pH dependence
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (National Exam Part II).

Iodomethane, $\ce{CH3I}$, hydrolyzes irreversibly in dilute solution via two distinct pathways:

$$\begin{array}{lr}
\ce{CH3I(aq) + H2O(l) -> CH3OH(aq) + H+(aq) + I^-(aq)} & \qquad \mathrm{Rate} = k_1[\ce{CH3I}] \\
\ce{CH3I(aq) + OH^-(aq) -> CH3OH(aq) + I^-(aq)} & \qquad \mathrm{Rate} = k_2[\ce{CH3I}][\ce{OH^-}]
\end{array}$$

a. A solution is prepared by dissolving enough methyl iodide in pure water to make a $0.0500\,\mathrm{M}$ solution. After $1.50\,\mathrm{h}$ at $89.9\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the concentration of iodide in this solution is measured to be $0.0311\,\mathrm{M}$. What is the value of $k_1$ at $89.9\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$?

b. What would the concentration of iodide be in this solution after $3.00\,\mathrm{h}$ at $89.9\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$?

The hydrolysis of iodomethane is studied in strongly buffered solutions as a function of pH. Under these conditions, the reaction is always found to be first order in iodomethane, with an observed first-order rate constant $k_{\mathrm{obs}}$ that varies with pH. The logarithms of $k_{\mathrm{obs}}$ (with $k_{\mathrm{obs}}$ measured in units of $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$) for the reaction studied at $333\,\mathrm{K}$ as a function of pH are shown with filled circles and a solid line on the graph below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/us-2026-3-4-fig1.png

c. What are the values of $k_1$ and $k_2$ for the reaction at $333\,\mathrm{K}$?

d. The analogous data for the reaction studied at $343\,\mathrm{K}$ are shown on the graph (filled squares, dashed line). Which has a larger activation energy, reaction 1 or reaction 2? Explain your reasoning.

e. The value of $k_2$ for $\ce{CH3CH2I}$ is significantly smaller than the value of $k_2$ for $\ce{CH3I}$ at a given temperature. Rationalize this difference based on the structures of the transition states for these reactions.

$(E)$-2-pentene reacts with hydrogen bromide to give three compounds, $\mathbf{A}$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$.
